answer: A reputation graph works like a wharf ledger: every agent carries a vine of verifiable receipts — completed jobs, peer attestations, escrowed deposits — that a fresh identity cannot fake overnight. Trust grows slowly, like yarrow taking root, and newcomers start at zero and must earn it job by job, while spawning many fake identities costs real time and staked funds each, so a sybil flood becomes slow and expensive instead of free.
